findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate docs/adr/0063-web-search-capability-security-posture.md in Scope (or explicitly justify no ADR change) since the rebar-owned DDGS boundary adds a new rebar-side mechanism and an injected sentinel on the local route the ADR designates as its contract.
evidence: ADR 0063:62-64 'The three bounds are the contract: widening any of them (raising the caps, adding a rebar-side fetcher that returns page bodies, or asserting domain filtering) reopens the exposure this ADR accepts under those specific limits and must be re-argued here.'
Plan Scope lists only capabilities.py, plan_review_T1.md, and test_web_tool_gating.py — ADR 0063 absent
Plan Approach adds a rebar-owned boundary that injects a rebar-authored sentinel record on the local route the ADR governs
findings.finding: ADR 0063 (docs/adr/0063-web-search-capability-security-posture.md) is a documented consumer of the local web-search boundary that the plan does not enumerate in Scope. The ADR declares the three bounds (volume/shape/authority) as 'the contract' and states that 'adding a rebar-side fetcher' or otherwise altering the local route 'reopens the exposure this ADR accepts ... and must be re-argued here.' The plan interposes a rebar-owned DDGS boundary that both suppresses backend failures (branch 1 -> []) and injects a rebar-AUTHORED record into the result stream (branch 2 sentinel). Whether or not this counts as 'widening,' it materially changes the local-route behavior the ADR governs and adds a new rebar-side mechanism on that route, yet the ADR is not listed among files to update.
scenarios: A future reader consults ADR 0063 for the authoritative local-route contract and finds it silent on the new rebar-side interposer and injected sentinel record
findings.suggested_fix: Add docs/adr/0063 to the Scope list with a one-line note recording that the local route now routes through a rebar-owned DDGS boundary that maps 'No results found.' to [] and injects a fail-safe WEB_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE sentinel, confirming this does not widen the volume/shape/authority bounds.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (and state in the plan, with an oracle) that the fields the T1 sentinel-recognition rule keys on — an empty href and the single-record count — are present in the model-visible tool output the agentic reviewer reads, or restate the recognition rule in terms of fields the reviewer can actually observe.
evidence: AC7: 'plan_review_T1.md recognizes the sentinel only when the result list has exactly one record, title exactly WEB_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE, and href exactly ""; oracle: file inspection plus a rubric unit test asserting those strings.'
The AC7 oracle asserts the rubric TEXT contains the strings, not that href/record-count are observable to the reviewer in the tool's rendered output.

AC3 validates the RETURN list via TypeAdapter(list[DuckDuckGoResult]); no AC confirms how those records are serialized/presented to the model, so the href='' and 'exactly one record' predicates the decision rule depends on are of unverified model-visibility.
T1 is execution_mode: agentic (plan_review_T1.md front-matter), so the reviewer acts on rendered tool output, not on the raw Python list.
findings.finding: The new T1 sentinel-recognition decision rule requires the reviewer to match on 'href exactly empty string' and 'exactly one record', but the plan never establishes that the pydantic-ai DuckDuckGo tool surfaces href and the record count in the MODEL-VISIBLE rendered tool output the agentic reviewer consumes; if the serialization drops an empty href, the reviewer cannot apply the gate the rubric mandates.
findings.location: Approach / Scope (plan_review_T1.md sentinel clause) and AC7
scenarios: pydantic-ai renders DuckDuckGo results in a format that omits or collapses an empty href, so the reviewer sees title=WEB_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE but cannot confirm href=='' and either under- or over-recognizes the sentinel
The single-record count is not distinguishable to the reviewer if results are rendered as prose rather than an enumerable list
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC (or extend AC7) whose oracle inspects the pydantic-ai DuckDuckGo tool's model-facing serialization to show href and record count reach the reviewer; if href is not reliably surfaced, key the rubric's sentinel gate on the observable fields (e.g. exact title plus the fixed body sentence 'Prior art could not be verified.') instead of href.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Approach section, state per-arm the disposition each DDGSException branch surfaces using an explicit disposition word (e.g. branch 1: a masked transient backend outage is surfaced as UNVERIFIED/non-authoritative rather than as retryable-or-absent; branch 2: fatal-for-this-review notice), so the fail-safe winner is documented against the masking risk.
evidence: 'str(exc) == "No results found." returns [] because empty results and backend failure are indistinguishable in ddgs for this message and the review must complete.'

The plan states the composite fail-safe winner ('worst case is fail-safe: T1 reports prior art unverified, not PASS') but does not attach an explicit disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) to the branch-1 arm where a real backend outage is masked as [].
findings.finding: Branch 1 maps a possibly-masked transient backend failure (DDGSException 'No results found.') to an empty list, but the plan never states, using an explicit disposition word, what disposition surfaces for that arm — a genuine transient/retryable backend outage is silently downgraded to 'zero results' with no per-arm disposition label.
findings.location: Approach (decided), branch 1; Scope bullet on capabilities.py
scenarios: A real transient DuckDuckGo backend outage that surfaces as DDGSException('No results found.') is treated identically to a genuinely empty search, so the reviewer sees zero results rather than a retryable/transient signal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the rebar-owned DDGS boundary decision and its ddgs-version-coupled 'No results found.' string dependency in a durable design note (ADR / AGENTS.md / module docstring).
evidence: 'Own the local web-search boundary in rebar. Add a small DDGS boundary object'
Branch 1 keys on str(exc) == "No results found.", tied to ddgs behavior at pydantic-ai 1.107.2
No scope bullet or AC mentions an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new rebar-owned boundary object (RebarBoundaryDDGS) that wraps an adopted library's client and hard-codes a version-coupled string match (str(exc) == 'No results found.' against pydantic-ai/ddgs 1.107.2). This is a novel architectural decision and a library-coupled literal, but the plan captures the rationale only in the plan text and the T1 rubric — no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update is scheduled to record why rebar now owns this seam or that branch-1 correctness depends on the exact ddgs message string.
scenarios: A future ddgs/pydantic-ai upgrade changes the empty-result message; branch 1 silently stops matching and all failures route to the sentinel (over-reporting 'unverified') with no documented note of the coupling
A later maintainer sees a rebar-owned DDGS wrapper with no captured rationale for why the library's own tool wasn't used directly
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope bullet to capture the decision in AGENTS.md or a module-level docstring: why rebar owns the DDGS boundary, that branch-1 matches the ddgs 1.107.2 empty message literal, and that any other message fails safe to the sentinel.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Establish which exception classes DDGS.text() can raise (confirm whether RatelimitException/TimeoutException and any transport-level errors subclass DDGSException) and state whether the boundary's `except` must be widened (e.g. also catch non-DDGSException client errors and route them to the fail-safe Branch 2 sentinel) so no local-search failure can escape to gate_dispatch and re-trigger gate-wide INDETERMINATE.
evidence: Approach: 'Its text(query, max_results=...) delegates to the real DDGS and catches ddgs.exceptions.DDGSException'
Root cause reproduced only 'DDGSException("No results found.")' — 'reproduced the escape as ddgs.exceptions.DDGSException'; no evidence the underlying client is limited to raising DDGSException
ddgs.exceptions.RatelimitException and ddgs.exceptions.TimeoutException both resolve in the env; whether they and any transport-level error are DDGSException subclasses is load-bearing and unstated
Problem statement: the whole point is that one uncaught local-search exception degrades a completed review to unsigned INDETERMINATE via LLMUnavailableError in gate_dispatch
findings.finding: The boundary catches only ddgs.exceptions.DDGSException, but the plan does not establish that the delegated DDGS.text() cannot raise a non-DDGSException error (e.g. a raw httpx/network/connection error from the underlying client). Any such escape would propagate through gate_dispatch and degrade the whole gate to INDETERMINATE — the exact defect this plan exists to eliminate.
findings.location: Approach (decided), step catching ddgs.exceptions.DDGSException; Root cause section
scenarios: ddgs raises a transport/connection error (or a non-DDGSException subclass) during a T1 prior-art sweep on a Bedrock model that has no native search route
A future ddgs version narrows what its text() wraps in DDGSException, letting a raw exception surface

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the exact-string match on the ddgs 'No results found.' message will stay durable (e.g. pin the ddgs version, add a drift test that fails if the upstream message changes, or document the fail-open consequence) so a future ddgs message change does not silently restore the abort-as-outage behavior.
evidence: Plan: 'str(exc) == "No results found." returns [] because empty results and backend failure are indistinguishable in ddgs for this message'

ddgs GitHub issue #427 confirms the exact message 'DDGSException: No results found.' is raised when a backend drops results — corroborating the plan but also showing the message is an upstream implementation detail, not a stable contract
AC1 pins the oracle to the literal DDGSException('No results found.') string, so a message drift is untested and would regress silently
findings.finding: Branch 1's empty-vs-failure classification depends on an exact string-equality match on the ddgs exception message ('No results found.'), an unverified-durability capability assertion: a future ddgs message/locale change would silently stop matching and restore the original abort-as-outage behavior.
scenarios: A ddgs upgrade rewords or localizes the 'No results found.' message
A different DDGSException subtype/message for a genuine backend failure falls through to branch 2 (sentinel) instead of branch 1
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note (and a small drift/oracle test) that the branch-1 match keys on the ddgs message string 'No results found.' as OBSERVED in the pinned ddgs version, and that any other DDGSException message deliberately routes to branch 2 (sentinel, fail-safe); if ddgs is upgraded, the message assumption must be re-verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the TypeAdapter(list[DuckDuckGoResult]) validation in AC3 is meant to guard upstream DuckDuckGoResult schema drift (not to re-check the boundary's own literals); if only the former, state that intent so the check reads as deliberate rather than reflexive validation.
evidence: Plan: 'Validate outputs with TypeAdapter(list[DuckDuckGoResult]).'
Both branches build their dicts from constants — branch 2 is title 'WEB_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE', href '', a computed body; branch 1 returns [].
search_files for 'TypeAdapter' across the repo returned (no matches) — this introduces a validation pattern with no existing call-site.
The stated intent is fail-safe, so the validation is low-cost and not a correctness risk.
findings.finding: AC3 mandates TypeAdapter(list[DuckDuckGoResult]) runtime validation of records the boundary itself constructs from fixed string literals, and TypeAdapter is used nowhere else in the codebase; validating self-built constants is largely belt-and-suspenders.
scenarios: The boundary returns its own fixed-literal sentinel, which cannot violate the schema unless the pydantic-ai DuckDuckGoResult TypedDict itself changes shape.
